citations.text: Hardin, G. (1968). The Tragedy of the Commons. Science, 162(3859), 1243-1248.
Ostrom, E. (1990). Governing the Commons: The Evolution of Institutions for Collective Action.

en.general: The social dilemma (OE-SANDBOX-CONCEPT-000016) that arises when individuals acting in their own rational self-interest deplete a shared, finite resource, even though this outcome harms the group's long-term interest, including the individuals' own (Hardin 1968). Hardin's original framing has been substantially qualified by later empirical work — notably Ostrom (1990) — showing that many communities avoid this outcome through self-governing institutions, without requiring privatization or external (state) control.

examples: Overfishing a shared fishery until fish stocks collapse.
Community-managed irrigation systems, forests, and fisheries that avoid collapse through locally-evolved rules and monitoring (Ostrom's counter-cases).
